name: JiraTaskCreation
description: Comment-driven Jira work-breakdown agent. Someone comments '@Aetherion <requirement>' on any Jira issue; the agent reads that comment as the request and the issue (description, attachments, other comments, links, history) as context, reviews every existing ticket in the project, then creates an Epic, User Stories and Sub-tasks. It replies on the same issue signed AetherionAgent, and emails when it needs clarification or found the work already exists. It never creates duplicates.

triggers.name: issue_key
triggers.description: Jira issue the request was made on, e.g. 'TT2-12'. Sent by the webhook receiver. The requirement, project and context are all read from this issue. Leave blank to run manually with the Requirement field instead.

triggers.name: comment_id
triggers.description: Id of the comment that asked. Sent by the webhook receiver so the right request is answered when several arrive together. Leave blank to answer the most recent unanswered request on the issue.

triggers.name: requirement
triggers.description: Manual mode only. The requirement to decompose when no Issue Key is supplied. Ignored when an Issue Key is given.

triggers.name: project_key
triggers.description: Manual mode only. Jira project key to create issues in, e.g. 'TT2'. In webhook mode this is taken from the issue itself.

triggers.name: project_name
triggers.description: Optional label for the project. Leave blank to use the name Jira already holds.

triggers.name: existing_epic_key
triggers.description: Optional. Key of an existing Epic, e.g. 'TT2-5'. New stories are added under it instead of creating a new Epic. Verified to exist, to be an Epic, and to belong to the chosen project.

triggers.name: placement
triggers.description: Where new stories go. Normally read from the request itself ('Add the stories to the current sprint'); set here to override. 'current_sprint' fails before creating anything if there is no single active sprint.

triggers.name: create_in_jira
triggers.description: When true (default), create the Jira issues after validation succeeds. Set to false to review the breakdown without writing anything.

triggers.name: force
triggers.description: Answer a request again even if it has already been answered, or run on an issue with no '@Aetherion' comment. Use to re-run by hand.

triggers.name: correlation_id
triggers.description: Optional external id used as the idempotency key, so re-running reuses the issues already created instead of duplicating them. Defaults to '<issue key>#<comment id>'.
